questions.learningObjective: Apply credit cards and revolving credit concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: A practical case: Layla Kaur receives $980 of monthly income and spends $49 on groceries. What percentage of income is that?

options.misconception: reports the dollar amount rather than the percentage share
divides the whole by the part instead of the part by the whole
forgets to multiply the fraction by one hundred

questions.explanation: The share is the part divided by the whole, then multiplied by one hundred. $49 divided by $980 is 0.05 as a decimal, so 5% of income goes to groceries. Dividing the other way or skipping the factor of one hundred gives a different, wrong figure.
questions.hint: Divide the expense by income, then convert to a percent.
